key_insight: Mixed IQP-QCBMs keep local trainability while gaining expressivity through branch specialization, but they improve only when branches separate into distinct modes rather than collapsing to the same distribution.
engineering_relevance: For quantum generative modeling, this suggests a practical route to scalable training: initialize branches to capture different data clusters so the circuit remains trainable and achieves better likelihood-style matching.
method: Generalize ancilla-extended IQP-QCBMs into a weighted mixture of ancilla-free IQP branches.
Prove local barren-plateau avoidance for polynomially many branches under data-agnostic and some data-dependent initializations.
Introduce cluster initialization to assign different unsupervised data clusters to different branches, encouraging mode separation.
evidence_signal: Exact 16-bit calculations and four benchmarks show cluster initialization converges fastest and achieves the lowest mean test MMD², with specialized branches matching distinct data features.
watch_item: Mode separation is difficult to obtain if branches start from nearly identical distributions, because the gradients needed to differentiate them are suppressed.
paper_title: Trainability and Mode Separation of Mixed IQP-QCBMs
